subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@fincloud.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T15:08:00-07:00
Subject: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Hi Samir — thanks again for the intro call today. Quick recap from my side so we have alignment and clear next steps. Happy to adjust if I missed anything.

Key pain points you shared:
- High monthly spend (~$120k) across OpenAI (chat & embeddings) and Anthropic (chat) with unpredictable cost spikes.
- Latency for customer-facing chat (p99 spikes to ~1s under load) impacting conversion for product search assistants.
- Vendor lock-in concerns — need API parity and a migration path off proprietary endpoints.
- Compliance: SOC 2 in-scope, retention and audit log requirements, and occasional EU-data residency needs.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Chat: Anthropic Claude (for longer-form assistant) + OpenAI chat models for quick interactions.
- Embeddings: OpenAI text-embedding-3-large for semantic search (batched offline & some online).
- Serving: internal microservices on GCP with a Redis KV cache for chat context.

Success criteria for a migration POC:
1) Cost: demonstrable per-token savings target (~>=40% unit cost reduction) while keeping overall infra cost predictable.
2) Performance: maintain or improve latency targets (p50 < 80ms, p95 < 200ms for short chat calls; p99 target < 300ms for core flows).
3) Quality: parity of responses — no more than 5% drop in key evaluation metrics on our 500-sample prompt set (relevance/QA and safety checks).
4) Compatibility: API surface that supports chat-style calls, streaming, function/tool calling (or clear mapping), and embedding shape/compatibility.
5) Compliance: demonstrable controls for audit logs and ability to deploy in a VPC/private environment.

Model shortlist (initial candidates we discussed):
- Llama 2 / Llama 3-family variants (instruction-tuned)
- Mistral Instruct / Mistral Mix variants
- Falcon / RedPajama derivatives for cost-sensitive embedding workloads
- Smaller distilled variants for low-latency endpoints and batching efficiency

Recommended next steps (mutual action plan):
- I attached a one-pager roadmap + mutual action plan (MAP-FinCloud-MAP.xlsx) with milestones for a 3-week POC: compatibility checklist, evaluation harness, and cost-runner.
- Schedule a technical deep-dive with Aditya (SE) to map API compatibility and infra requirements — target next week.
- Security check: Vivek will follow up on SOC2/audit evidence and data residency questions.

Attachments: redwood-migration-roadmap.pdf; MAP-FinCloud-MAP.xlsx

Proposed times for the deep-dive: Tue/Wed next week (10:00-12:30 PT window works for us). Please confirm what works for you and if Olivia should join the technical session.

Thanks again — excited to help FinCloud reduce costs and remove lock-in risk.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference

From: Samir Gupta <samir@fincloud.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Olivia Price <olivia@fincloud.com>
Date: 2026-03-20T15:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: migration off proprietary LLM APIs

Thanks Marissa — this is a great write-up and captures everything. A few clarifications and additions from our side:

- Embeddings volume: we batch ~1.2M docs monthly (weekly reindex + nearline updates) and run online similarity for recent items. OpenAI embeddings are the largest single cost driver.
- Chat usage: ~60% of queries are short clarifications (<=40 tokens generated), 40% are longer threads used by our customer success bots. We use both OpenAI and Anthropic depending on the flow.
- Compliance: SOC2 is table-stakes. We also have an external audit every 18 months; any migration needs to be auditable with retained request logs for 24 months.
- Acceptance criteria: in addition to Marissa's bullets, we need clear anti-regression checks for hallucination on our 500-sample safety/test set.

Questions for the technical deep-dive:
1) How does Redwood handle function-calling parity (we have a number of system tools that expect structured JSON returns)?
2) Can you map how embedding vector dimensions and refresh semantics would work with open models (we can't sacrifice downstream search quality)?
3) Any initial ideas on a cost model for serving embeddings vs. chat (batch vs. online)?

We can do Tue 2026-03-24 10:30 PT for the deep-dive — Olivia and I will be on. Appreciate the MAP — will review and provide comments by EOD Monday.

Best,
Samir
VP Product, FinCloud
samir@fincloud.com
